note: Config Override Core Fields is a data-provider only: one hook_form_alter() tags elements on a fixed list of core config forms with $element['#config']['key'] = 'config.object:key' (e.g. system.site:name, system.performance:cache.page.max_age). No config, no schema, no permissions, no plugins, no configure route. Consumers (notably COI) read those hints. Medium cases confirm the isset()-guarded mappings that only appear when a contrib module is enabled (dblog.settings:row_limit on the logging form, automated_cron.settings:interval on the cron form) - genuine live-state. Hard cases have the agent write a core config value via the object/key that a given site-info field maps to (system.site:slogan, system.site:page.403), verified on the live config; reset/cleanup restore the shipped-empty defaults.

evals.prompt: What does the config_override_core_fields module actually do to Drupal's core configuration forms, and in which render-array property does it record the mapping? Does it provide any user-facing feature on its own?
evals.expected_output: Its single hook_form_alter() tags core config-form elements with $element['#config']['key'] = '<config_object>:<dotted.key>' (e.g. system.site:name). It has no feature of its own; it just provides these hints for a consumer like COI (which also honors the core WIP #config_data_store['key']).

evals.prompt: On the Basic site settings form (system_site_information_settings), config_override_core_fields maps the 'Site name' field to a configuration object and key. What is that config key string?
evals.expected_output: The site_name element gets #config['key'] = 'system.site:name'. (Related keys on the same form: system.site:slogan, system.site:mail, system.site:page.front, system.site:page.403/404.)

evals.prompt: This site has the Database Logging (dblog) module enabled, so its 'Database log messages to keep' field appears on the logging settings form. Using config_override_core_fields' mapping, determine the config object and key that this row-limit field is annotated with, and report it.
evals.expected_output: config_override_core_fields maps the dblog_row_limit field on system_logging_settings to #config['key'] = 'dblog.settings:row_limit' (guarded by isset, so it only applies when dblog is enabled).

evals.prompt: The Automated Cron module is enabled on this site, so the cron settings form shows a 'Run cron every' interval field. Per config_override_core_fields, which configuration object and key is that interval field mapped to?
evals.expected_output: On system_cron_settings the interval field gets #config['key'] = 'automated_cron.settings:interval' (added only when automated_cron is enabled, via an isset guard).

evals.prompt: config_override_core_fields maps the 'Slogan' field on the Basic site settings form to a specific configuration object and key. Using that exact mapping, set the site slogan to 'COCF Verified Slogan' by writing to the correct config object/key, and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: system.site:slogan is set to 'COCF Verified Slogan' (the config object/key the slogan field maps to), e.g. drush config:set system.site slogan 'COCF Verified Slogan'.

evals.prompt: On the Basic site settings form the '403 (access denied) page' field is mapped by config_override_core_fields to a config object and key. Using that mapping, set the 403 page path to '/cocf-403' by writing the correct config object/key on the live site.
evals.expected_output: system.site:page.403 is set to '/cocf-403' (the config object/key the 403 field maps to), e.g. drush config:set system.site page.403 '/cocf-403'.
